q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis: NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution

Today is 2026-08-21. Q2 FY2027 would typically conclude around July/August 2026, with earnings released shortly thereafter. Given the research indicates guidance was issued on May 20, 2026, we are **already past the earnings announcement date**. The guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue has already been issued at **$91.0 billion ± 2%**.

However, interpreting the question literally: it asks "What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release?" This appears to be asking for the actual guidance figure that was/will be provided, not a forecast of what it will be.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The research explicitly states NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue issued on May 20, 2026: **$91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%**.

This means:
- **Midpoint: $91.0 billion**
- **Upper bound (~2% above): $92.8 billion**
- **Lower bound (~2% below): $89.2 billion**

The guidance is definitive and was already issued. The most likely outcome is that the actual reported guidance figure is the stated $91.0 billion midpoint.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- If the actual reported revenue came in at the **lower bound** of the ±2% range: **$89.2 billion**
- Potential headwinds: China export restrictions tightening further, unexpected demand softness, customer pushback on pricing, or macro slowdown

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- If the actual reported revenue came in at the **upper bound** of the ±2% range: **$92.8 billion**
- Potential tailwinds: Stronger than expected AI/data center demand, broader adoption of new products, less severe China restrictions than anticipated, or pricing power advantages

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research provides specific prior data: NVIDIA reported $46.7 billion in the year-ago quarter, and the guidance represents an implied doubling. This is consistent with NVIDIA's extraordinary growth trajectory in the AI era. The guidance midpoint of $91.0 billion represents approximately 95% year-over-year growth, which aligns with documented market expectations for NVIDIA's AI-driven expansion.

---

Since the guidance has already been issued at $91.0 billion (with a ±2% range), my estimate for the reported forward guidance figure is centered on this stated amount:

Low (10th percentile): 89200000000
Median (50th percentile): 91000000000
High (90th percentile): 92800000000

NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, predicts $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This guidance explicitly assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). The midpoint of this range is $91.0 billion, with a ceiling near $92.8 billion and a floor near $89.2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

Wall Street analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is approximately $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), which falls within NVIDIA's guided range and is about 1% above the company's midpoint [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This guidance represents an implied year-over-year revenue increase close to doubling from the $46.7 billion reported in the year-ago quarter
